summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy was admitted due to worsening throat pain, brown tracheostomy secretions with occasional blood, and increased mucus plugging. She had recently started oral doxycycline for MRSA tracheitis identified on bronchial washings but developed significant nausea, prompting a switch to IV doxycycline. She denied fever or chest pain but reported chills and shortness of breath. Evaluation showed no leukocytosis, no growth on blood cultures, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Her symptoms improved with IV antibiotics and pain management. She was discharged home with a five-day course of IV doxycycline via PICC line, continued home medications, and home health support.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
